summary: George Berrington worked through Larkspur's open opportunities with Joanna Pike and Oliver Grant. The spreadsheet tracker had 31 rows with no stage definitions and several deals untouched for months. We agreed five stages with exit criteria tied to the operating partner discovery from Week 4, and a rule for stalled deals.

discussion.keyPoints: Of 31 open rows, Oliver judged only 11 to be live. Several were corporate assessment enquiries from last year that nobody had closed off.
Joanna estimated a 40% win rate on proposals, but Larkspur has no data on how many conversations become proposals. George noted this hides where deals actually drop out.
Integration work moves fast around completion dates, while retainers will likely take longer. Joanna was concerned about forecasting retainers at all.

recommendations.recommendation: Adopt five stages: Conversation, Discovery held, Proposal sent, Verbal yes, Signed, with Discovery held requiring the operating partner present.
Close any opportunity with no client contact for 45 days and move it to a nurture list.
Hold 3 times quarterly fee target in qualified pipeline, around 540k GBP against a 180k GBP quarter.
Track conversion stage by stage from next month, aiming for 50% Discovery to Proposal.

actions.action: Clean the tracker down to the 11 live opportunities and re-stage them

nextFocus: Choose a CRM and decide which metrics and dashboards the partners will review.
nextPreparation: Joanna to confirm budget for a CRM licence for 15 users.

tests.question: What pipeline stages did we agree?
What is our rule for stalled deals?
Is the pipeline coverage target agreed?
